INDEPENDENT CRITICAL SEPARABILITY AUDIT — 7 October 2026
Worker: /root/critical_separability_audit

VERDICT AND EXACT SCOPE

The O(N^(-3/2)) whole-density distance to the fully separable cone passes this
independent audit. It is an internally proved candidate, not external validation
or historical-priority clearance. The construction is a mixture of IDENTICAL
single-qubit products, stronger than arbitrary fully separable mixtures.

The latest child proof also supplies a parameter-independent fully separable
reverse channel for the unknown critical A,b experiment. I independently checked
Addendum C, including its concentration/moment/normalization steps. Its error is
O(N^(-1/4)); the weighted scalar Laplace remainder is O(N^(-1/2)). It does NOT
inherit the N^(-3/2) rate. The faster approximation depends on the actual A,b.

A real-arithmetic known-parameter sampler can be made explicit with
O_(M,B)(eta^(-3)+N) expected scalar work/local preparations, plus public finite-N
certificate evaluation, for error E_N+O(eta). This report supplies a seed rejection
sampler and uniform weight-moment constants. A finite-bit implementation, certified
quadrature library and gate compiler have not been built or verified.

real b with |b|<=B; public fixed finite bounds M,B. Target

FULL SEPARABILITY AUDIT — completed internal derivation, 7 October 2026
Worker: /root/spin_glass_physics/full_separability_audit

STATUS: internally derived theorem candidate. The finite-N fully separable bound
and universal product decoder have passed a separate internal proof audit. A
complete real-arithmetic preparation construction is also provided below, with
sampling/discretization costs charged. Historical priority, external correctness,
and an implemented finite-bit compiler remain unestablished. No numerical check
supplies any step of the proof.

Three different conclusions must be retained:
  (i) a parameter-dependent iid-product mixture is O(N^(-3/2)) from rho;
  (ii) the parameter-INDEPENDENT iid-product decoder from one quartic observation
       has uniform O(N^(-1/4)) error;
  (iii) known-parameter preparation to error E_N+2eta costs O_(M,B)(eta^(-3))
       classical normal/scalar work plus N local qubit emissions, in the declared
       real-arithmetic model. None of these rates is proved optimal.

STRONGEST RESULT
For fixed public M,B<infinity, A=A^T real with ||A||op<=M and |b|<=B, put
  J_i=(1/2)sum_(a=1)^N sigma_i^(a), s=N^(3/4),
  K=2J^2/N+Q_A(J)/N^(3/2)+b.J/s,
  rho=exp(K)/Tr exp(K), T(rho,sigma)=||rho-sigma||_1/2.
For every N with t0=2/N-M/N^(3/2)>0 there is an explicit state sigma,
which is a convex mixture of IDENTICAL single-qubit products tau^(tensor N),
such that
  sup_(A,b) T(rho,sigma) <= min{1, E_N(M,B)},
  E_N(M,B) = [3M/(2N^(3/2))] U_N(M,B)/D_N(M,B),                 (1)
where entirely public finite binomial sums define the quantities on the right:
  j=j_min,j_min+1,...,N/2; j_min=0 even N, 1/2 odd N,
  d_j=2j+1,
  m_N(j)=d_j/(N+1) binom(N+1,N/2-j),
  a_N(j)=d_j m_N(j) exp[2j(j+1)/N],
  r_j=(j+1/2)/s,
  D_N=sum_j a_N(j) exp[-M r_j^2-B r_j],
  P(r)=4M r^2+(B/2)r+(4M r^2+B r)^2/3,
  U_N=sum_j a_N(j) exp[M r_j^2+B r_j] P(r_j).
The quotient U_N/D_N is bounded for all sufficiently large N, for each fixed
M,B. Consequently the approximation error is O_(M,B)(N^(-3/2)). For M=0
the construction is exact. This is a fully separable whole-density result,
stronger than a statement concerning two-spin reductions or collective moments.

CONSTRUCTIVE FINITE-PRECISION BOOKKEEPING — 7 October 2026
Worker: /root/spin_glass_physics. Internally derived; independent internal audit
PASS saved in work/cycle1/spin_finite_precision_audit.txt. Final finite-decision
repairs requested by that audit are incorporated below. No external validation.
This is a mathematical finite-bit approximation of Addendum D of
spin_full_separability_audit.txt. No certified implementation or hardware run is
claimed. It does not change the already independently audited real-arithmetic
sampler. All input/acquisition and native quantum-gate assumptions are stated.

INPUT MODEL
N is an integer. A,b,M,B are known rational data of total bit length Lin, with
the stated norm bounds. Alternatively coefficient precision can be supplied by
an interface whose actual evaluation cost is charged explicitly; polynomial
total bit cost then requires that interface to be polynomial-time. Arbitrary
noncomputable real parameters have no finite-bit algorithmic claim. A native
one-qubit preparation can be specified by a finite
classical rotation angle and a finite classical Bernoulli probability; errors in
the resulting one-qubit density are charged, rather than assumed zero.

Fix rational/dyadic eta,epsilon in (0,1/4), charging their representation lengths
as part of total input length. Use the finite sampler's public m,R
(R=Rprop), with
error Esep_N+2eta before numerical approximation. Let p0=L0/Cg>0 be its proven
seed rejection acceptance lower bound, and let sigma_max=768^(1/4)/sqrt(2),
the larger standard deviation in its two-Maxwell prior proposal. All requested
ceilings/thresholds are computed from CERTIFIED RATIONAL UPPER BOUNDS, with a
fixed slack, on F_N, K2star, 1/p0, log expressions and precision quantities.
No exact comparison with a transcendental integer boundary is requested. For
example Fbar_N can be enclosed with F_N<=Fbar_N<=F_N+1, then
m=max{1,ceil(Fbar_N/eta)}. The Gamma(3/4) in K2star can simply be replaced by
the proven bound Gamma(3/4)<=4/3+exp(-1)<2. These choices preserve the stated
O_(M,B) scales while allowing conservative finite rational computation.
